```{r, include=F}
library(foreign)
library(tidyverse)
articles <- read.dta("http://www.stata-press.com/data/lf2/couart2.dta")

m_art <- glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, 
             family = poisson, data = articles)
#summary(m_art)
```

## Overdispersion

**Overdispersion** occurs when the response variable $Y_i$ has greater variability than the model accounts for.

\vspace{1cm}

**Poisson:** $Var(Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i) = \mathbb{E}[Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i] = \mu_i$

\bigskip

If we fit a Poisson regression model, overdispersion means that $Var(Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i) > \mu_i$

\vspace{2cm}

## Behavior of estimated coefficients in a mis-specified model

## quasi-Poisson models

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log(\mu_i) &= \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta} \\
Var(Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i) &= \phi \mu_i
\end{aligned}
$$

\bigskip

* Estimated coefficients ($\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$) are the same
* Different estimated variance-covariance matrix

\vspace{4cm}

## Example: articles data

```{r, eval=F}
glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, family = poisson, data = articles)
```

```
             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
(Intercept)  0.276493   0.087294   3.167  0.00154 ** 
phd          0.008071   0.026358   0.306  0.75944    
ment         0.026537   0.002001  13.264  < 2e-16 ***
kid5        -0.099696   0.035248  -2.828  0.00468 ** 
(Dispersion parameter for poisson family 
   taken to be 1)
```

```{r, eval=F}
glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, family = quasipoisson, data = articles)
```

```
             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)  0.276493   0.119839   2.307   0.0213 *  
phd          0.008071   0.036184   0.223   0.8235    
ment         0.026537   0.002747   9.662   <2e-16 ***
kid5        -0.099696   0.048389  -2.060   0.0397 *  
(Dispersion parameter for quasipoisson family 
   taken to be 1.88461)
```

## Activity: comparing standard errors

Options for estimating $SE(\widehat{\beta}_j)$ when we fit a Poisson model:

* Estimate from the original Poisson model (may be wrong!)
* Bootstrap resampling (should be approximately correct even if model is misspecified)
* Sandwich variance (should be approximately correct even if model is misspecified)
* quasi-Poisson (inflate standard errors by $\sqrt{\widehat{\phi}}$)


## Activity: comparing standard errors

* Poisson estimate: $\widehat{SE}(\widehat{\beta}_3)_{\text{poisson}} = 0.03525$
* Bootstrap estimate: $\widehat{SE}(\widehat{\beta}_3)_{\text{boot}} = 0.0490$
* Sandwich estimate: $\widehat{SE}(\widehat{\beta}_3)_{\text{sandwich}} = 0.0483$
* quasi-Poisson estimate: $\widehat{SE}(\widehat{\beta}_3)_{\text{quasi-poisson}} = 0.0484$

\bigskip

How do the estimates compare? What will be the effect (on confidence intervals and hypothesis tests) of incorrectly assuming a Poisson distribution when the data are overdispersed?
